mode: real loopback HTTP; standalone backends; anonymous journeys

toolchains.rust: Rust 1.98.1 release thin-LTO final Tokio 2 workers and 2 blocking threads

notes: Six requests per Intrusul journey: create, resume, wrong tap, hint, win, terminal resume; score 650.
Identical measured seed sequence, content manifest, CPUs and client checks for every target; full normalized response traces must match.
Selected target orders rotate across repeats; every run uses a new backend process without a Python proxy for native servers.
Warmup and startup are excluded from elapsed time and backend CPU. Worker HTTP connections remain open into measurement.
Backend affinity is reset by taskset; client threads inherit the separately reported client affinity. On a host with only two allowed CPUs they share.
Backend CPU is /proc/pid/stat utime+stime; parent/client CPU is reported separately and excluded.
Idle RSS is after warmup; sampled peak is measurement-only; process lifetime HWM also includes startup/warmup.
Latency measures complete HTTP response transfer before client JSON decoding; percentiles use nearest rank.
Fixed-load throughput may be limited by this client or other host activity; it is not maximum server capacity.
Selected processes load the full six-game graph and bounded sessions; native servers have no Python upstream.
These measurements establish neither hosting-plan capacity nor percentage hosting savings.
